title: No infinite regress of divine testimonies — must stop somewhere
source_text: XXIV. Nec etiam hic recurrere potest ad alterum quoddam Dei testimonium quo Dei verbum innotescat. Nam una quidem verbi divini pars potest alteri parti testimonium perhibere, & una revelatio per aliam confirmari, atque innotescere, quemadmodum Novum Testamentum testimonium Veteri perhibet, & authoritatem illius confirmat. Sed hic dari non potest progressus in infinitum, & sistendum est tandem in aliquo Dei testimonio, in quo mens acquiescat, & quod non debeat per prius aliud innotescere.
pass_a_gloss: Nor also here can one run back to some other testimony of God by which God’s word becomes known. For one part of the divine word can indeed bear testimony to another part, and one revelation be confirmed and made known through another — as the New Testament bears testimony to the Old and confirms its authority. But here a progress to infinity cannot be given, and at last one must stop in some testimony of God in which the mind rests, and which ought not to become known through some prior other.
pass_b_english: Cannot solve by another prior divine testimony ad infinitum.
NT can confirm OT — parts witness to parts.
Must stop in some divine testimony where the mind rests without prior other.

lemmas.latin: sistendum est tandem in aliquo Dei testimonio
lemmas.gloss: at last one must stop in some testimony of God

rejected: each divine word needs a prior divine word to innotesce
